title: Yarra: A Novel of Tangkhul Youth and Spring Awakening
alternate_titles: Yarra: The Springtime of Naga Youth
Friendship, Music, and Courtship in the Highland Hills
subject: Novel (Upanyas), Youth Culture & Traditional Music
notes: Vibrant lyrical novel depicting 'Yarra' (traditional Tangkhul youth club/dormitory culture), folk song creation, courtship dialogues, and communal loyalty.

front_matter.title_page: Yarra: A Novel of Tangkhul Youth and Spring Awakening (2002)
front_matter.preface: Yarra celebrates the age-grade youth institutions (Longshim and Yarra) that formed the social and moral backbone of traditional Tangkhul society. The novel captures the humor, musical creativity, and peer solidarity that flourished in these dormitory fellowships.

chapters.title: The Longshim Fellowship (Youth Dormitory Life)
chapters.summary: Life inside the traditional Tangkhul dormitory where storytelling, oral lore, and discipline were taught.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Ngazing shoklakha, village-wui yaronaobingna Longshimli (youth dormitory) pamkazipsaye. Eldersbingna athumli ancestral wari, customary laws, kala archery training miye. Tingteila kala siphung flute kakhong eina athumna traditional laa tuitam khuiye. Longshim china youth-li discipline kala clan solidarity kasakakhui shim thada leisai.
chapters.english_translation: At nightfall, village youths gathered in the Longshim (communal youth dormitory). Elders instructed them in ancestral chronicles, customary laws, and the art of archery. With tambourines and bamboo flutes, they rehearsed traditional folk songs. The Longshim served as a sacred academy of character, discipline, and communal solidarity.

vocabulary.meaning: traditional communal youth dormitory / cultural academy

exercises: Describe the pedagogical role of the Longshim in ancient Tangkhul villages.
Identify the musical instruments played during dormitory evenings.

chapters.title: The Courtship Songs of Spring (Yarra Laa)
chapters.summary: Antiphonal courtship singing during the clearing of agricultural paths.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: Zingyur atamli, mayarnaobing kala ngalanaobingna shongfa shomlakha Yarra Laa honserie. Mayarnaobingna call verses honsanglaga, ngalanaobingna response verses mathat-eina ngahanmi. Tuiwon kaphā eina athum romantic affection chitheiye; kha customary modesty (Kashan) kuppup preserve saye.
chapters.english_translation: In the spring season, as young men and women cleared the mountain footpaths together, they sang the antiphonal Yarra songs. The youths launched poetic call verses, and the maidens responded in graceful rhyming counterpoint. Through elegant metaphors they conveyed romantic admiration while preserving strict customary modesty.

vocabulary.meaning: traditional youth courtship and work song

grammar_notes: Antiphonal singing syntax: call and response clauses.
exercises: Translate a stanza of Yarra Laa into English.

chapters.title: The Harvest Feast & Lifelong Bonds
chapters.summary: The youth celebrate the harvest festival, transitioning into responsible adult householders.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: Chumpha harvest festival shoklakha, Yarra group-na village-li community service salaga feast kasaye. Mayarnaobing kala ngalanaobingna marriage eina household kathara phokserie. Longshimwui friendship thot pupup athum lungli leirap sara.
chapters.english_translation: When the Chumpha harvest festival arrived, the youth association rendered community service and held a celebratory feast. Betrothed couples stepped forward into honorable marriage and established new households. The deep bonds forged in the Longshim remained unbroken throughout their adult lives.

vocabulary.meaning: traditional harvest festival of granary sanctification

grammar_notes: Rites of passage vocabulary: moving from youth dormitory to independent householding.
exercises: How does the novel depict the social transition from youth to adulthood?
